simple: Imperva’s on-premises WAF (a Thales company) for applications that can’t or shouldn’t move to the cloud and for data-residency requirements: a hardware appliance (from 500 Mbps to 10 Gbps, with redundant power supplies and drives and fail-open interfaces) or a virtual one — in virtualization or IaaS cloud. Dynamic profiling learns the application and user behavior on its own and builds an “allowed” model, so it protects even complex non-standard systems; it combines this with signatures and correlation of violations to spot multi-stage attacks. Protects websites and APIs from OWASP Top 10 attacks and is managed through Terraform. Its events and those of the cloud WAF are collected in Attack Analytics. On the larger models, Imperva database activity monitoring and database firewall can run on the same platform — these are separate products. Imperva reputation threat intelligence is a separate subscription.
